title: Add the right indexes

checks.name: orders has an index on customer_id
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) >= 1 FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'orders' AND indexdef ~ '\(customer_id\)'

checks.name: books has an index on (genre, price), in that order
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) >= 1 FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'books' AND indexdef ~ '\(genre, price\)'

checks.name: authors has a unique index on name
checks.query: SELECT COUNT(*) >= 1 FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'authors' AND indexdef ~ '^CREATE UNIQUE INDEX' AND indexdef ~ '\(name\)'

checks.name: a second author with an existing name is now rejected
checks.query: INSERT INTO authors (id, name, country) VALUES (99, 'Mara Lind', 'Norway')

checks.name: the planner can use the index on orders
checks.query: SET enable_seqscan = off; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 3;

hints: A two-column index lists both columns in the brackets. The order matters: (genre, price).
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... makes the index enforce uniqueness as well.
